_comment: Sourced from Figma 'Lumen-AI-Design-System' file, page 'Design Tokens' > '01 Colors' (fileKey GJBYRm6ySR7XIECFcHMgy2, node 426:4396). Every family uses a 9-step ramp: 50/100/200/300/400/500/600/700/800, where 500 is the Figma 'Default' step. Read swatch fill colors, not the printed hex labels — several 'Default' rows in the source file have mislabeled caption text (a copy/paste artifact) though the swatches themselves render correctly. CORRECTION 2026-08-02: an earlier version of this comment claimed 'cobalt', 'japonica', 'deep-purple', 'forest', 'purple', 'pink', 'sand', and 'lemon-green' were all verified via a Figma Variables export — a live screenshot of Figma's actual Variables panel today shows most of these are not current Figma collections at all. 'japonica' and 'sand'/'lemon-green' (fully unconsumed) were deleted outright. 'cobalt', 'deep-purple', 'purple', and 'pink' are still consumed by semantic/color.json's Badge and toaster-systeminfo-bg roles, so they're kept for now but flagged PENDING REPLACEMENT on each family's own `_comment` — treat their hex values as unverified legacy, not Figma-sourced, until real values are supplied. That same publish also exposed 'Gray'/'Foundation' variable collections that duplicate 'neutral' step-for-step and a 'Lumen Crimson' collection duplicating 'primary' step-for-step — flagged then as unresolved naming collisions pending a canonical-name decision. RESOLVED (already, before this comment was even written, per docs/changelog.md's 'Resolved the Gray/Foundation vs. Neutral and Lumen Crimson vs. Primary naming collisions' entry, and reconfirmed 2026-08-04): those three were retired from Figma outright, not kept as a second canonical name — 'neutral'/'primary' are the only real collections and already match step-for-step, zero drift. A 2026-08-04 live check confirms today's file has exactly 3 variable collections (Primitives, Lumen/Theme, Typography) and no separate Gray/Foundation/Lumen Crimson collection at all. 2026-08-02: a fresh full Variables export (Primitives/Default + Lumen-Theme Light+Dark + Typography Desktop/Tablet/Mobile modes) added 900/950 tail steps to most existing 9-step ramps (exact matches for 50-800 on every family re-verified), plus two entirely new families ('lumen-dark', 'nightshade' below) that back most of the Dark theme's semantic aliases in semantic/color.json — see that file's own updated comment for the full list of newly-added semantic roles this unblocks. A third claimed family, 'icon-gray' (default/hover/selected), was removed the same day once the user reported it wasn't a real Figma collection either — its 'default'/'hover' values were exact duplicates of 'nightshade.400'/'nightshade.300', so its two consumers (icon.nav-default/nav-hover, dark theme) were repointed straight at nightshade instead. FINAL RECONCILIATION 2026-08-02, against the actual raw 'Default.tokens.json' Primitives/Default export the user pasted directly (not a screenshot): this is authoritative and resolves the pending flags. 'purple', 'deep-purple', and 'pink' ARE real Figma collections after all (present under those exact names, values matching what was already here) — their PENDING REPLACEMENT flags are removed; 'deep-purple'/'pink' also gained real 900/950 steps this export evidences that weren't here before. 'cobalt' is also absent from this comprehensive dump (which does include every other unusual hue — Deep Purple, Pink, Purple, Teal, Light Blue — so its absence is a real signal, not an export-scope gap); the user confirmed removing it outright rather than leaving it flagged. Its 3 consumers in semantic/color.json (light.background.badge, dark.background.badge, light.app-shell.badge-bg — none consumed by any actual UI component) were repointed to `blue`, resolving a gap semantic/color.json's own comment had already flagged: the Light theme export's own `bg.badge` variable was already known to resolve to `Blue/50` (#EAF0FD), left unrepointed at the time only because it looked 'close but not identical' to `cobalt.50` — with cobalt now confirmed fake, `blue.50` is the real answer. Dark mirrors to `blue.800`, following this file's own established X.50-light/X.800-dark 'subtle' pairing convention used by every other status-subtle pair. 'primary.10' (#F5EFF3) and 'neutral.250'/'neutral.850' are also absent from this export's otherwise-complete Primary/Neutral collections and had zero consumers anywhere in the codebase, so all three were deleted outright. 'nightshade.350'/'nightshade.850' are likewise absent from this export's complete Nightshade collection, but ARE consumed (background.code, background.brand-tint, border.toaster, dark theme) — kept but flagged PENDING REPLACEMENT rather than deleted. Two real new nightshade steps this export evidences were added: '100' (#E1DBDF) and '500' (#917D89). A new 'status.info' primitive (#0B8A3E) was also added from this export's 'Status' collection — flagged as it's byte-identical to 'status.green', likely a Figma-side copy/paste artifact; not wired to anything, and distinct from the unrelated semantic 'status.info' token (which resolves to blue.500).

primary._comment: This is also the brand ramp — primary.500 (#BE003C) is the Lumen brand color, shown separately as 'Brand Color' in the source file. That same export corrected the two translucent alpha steps below: 500-a10 (10%) and 300-a24 (24%) were re-verified against a fresh get_variable_defs pull and are actually 500-a8 (8%) and 300-a20 (20%) — renamed and re-pointed at their two consumers in semantic/color.json (light.button.secondary-bg, dark.button.secondary-bg) rather than left as a silently-wrong value under the old name. A 'primary.10' (#F5EFF3) step was added the same day but later deleted once a raw Default.tokens.json Primitives dump showed the real 'Primary' collection runs 25→950 with no '10' step — it had zero consumers, so no replacement was needed. REMOVED 2026-08-03: '300-a20'/'300-a40' were deleted at explicit user instruction after three consecutive Default.tokens.json 'Alpha' collection exports consistently omitted any '-300-'/'-400-' entries, only ever exposing the systematic 8/16/24/40/60/80% tint set at the '500' step (matching the standardized pattern already established for every other family). `dark.button.secondary-border` (was `300-a40`, exactly 40%) repoints to `500-a40`, an exact match. `dark.button.secondary-bg` (was `300-a20`, 20%) repoints to `500-a24` — the standardized set has no 20% step, and 20 is numerically equidistant between the 16/24 steps; 24 was chosen as the closer proportional match (20/16=1.25x vs 24/20=1.2x), not a further-evidenced value.

blue._comment: Added 2026-07-20 under the name 'sky', sourced from the canonical 'AppShell' page (node 1007:3700, Breakpoint=Desktop/Theme=Light instance 1127:4196) via get_variable_defs: the `text/link` variable (#2563EB) used for breadcrumb and footer inline links in that context. Only the 500 step was evidenced then. This file already had an older, differently-valued 'blue' family (500=#0E17FF) at the time, so the new ramp was added under a placeholder name ('sky') rather than colliding with it. Full ramp added 2026-08-02 from a fresh Variables export's 'Blue' family (50-950), which resolves 500 to this exact same #2563EB. That same day, the old #0E17FF 'blue' family's only two consumers (`status.info-subtle`) were repointed here and the old family was deleted, freeing the real name — but the placeholder 'sky' name was mistakenly kept a little longer. RENAMED 'sky' -> 'blue' the same day, once a live screenshot of Figma's own Variables panel confirmed the canonical group name is 'Blue' (11 variables) — there is no 'Sky' collection in Figma at all. Every reference across semantic/color.json and Storybook was updated in the same pass; do not reintroduce a 'sky' key. This is also the color that resolves 'status.info' in the Light+Dark theme export uniformly (non-theme-adaptive) and 'toast.info-accent' in semantic/color.json, closing the drift figma-sync.md's manifest previously flagged. code._comment: Exact code-block colors sourced from the 'AI Response Components' frame (node 1484:2905), via get_variable_defs, 2026-07-29. `bg` (`bg/code`) is theme-invariant — code blocks stay dark for contrast regardless of the app's light/dark mode, the same convention most code editors and this Figma frame use; there is no separate light/dark instance to evidence a different value. `syntax-keyword`/`syntax-string` are the only two Prism token colors this frame evidences (SQL keywords and string literals); every other syntax-highlighting token color (comment, number, function, etc.) has no Figma evidence and is deliberately left at the default text color in `CodeBlock`'s theme rather than invented.
